hero.label: Engineer → Founder → AI product and deployment
hero.headline: I spent seven years building an AI tutoring company from the ground up.
hero.intro: I founded LessonWise, took it through three pivots, and shipped BrightPath: a tutoring service where AI analyses every lesson and a human signs it off. This site shows how I work.

journey.heading: From drilling machines to machine learning.
journey.intro: I trained as a mechanical engineer, taught maths for a decade, and built a company in between. The thread is the same: find the real problem, then build the thing that solves it.

items.title: Design engineer at Herrenknecht
items.text: Designed drilling systems and machine elements, and delivered client projects to specification, working in German.

items.title: A music degree, and the start of teaching
items.text: Moved to London to study music and began tutoring maths. More than 4,000 hours of one-to-one teaching since.

items.title: LessonWise: a platform for tutors to teach groups online
items.text: Wrote the first product requirements, ran a tender, and led an offshore team to launch: virtual classroom, payments, homework and messaging. About 200 tutors joined within months.

items.title: Tutors did not want to build their own audience
items.text: So we found the students for them. Free masterclasses fed paid courses, and more than 4,000 students joined within four months.

items.title: One-to-one first
items.text: Narrowed the offer to one-to-one tuition to build a base of families who trusted us before going wider.

items.title: Back to a team of one, then up again
items.text: Ran the company alone for months, teaching and selling myself. Found an acquisition channel that worked, hired a sales team and grew revenue again.

items.title: BrightPath: managed tutoring with AI in every lesson
items.text: Short-term exam customers did not stay. I redesigned the business around families who wanted their child's learning managed, on subscription, with evidence of progress every month.

items.title: BrightPath live with paying families
items.text: In September 2026 I handed the company to a new leadership team. It continues today as Alucea.

work.heading: Four problems, and how I solved them.
work.intro: Each one covers the problem, the decisions I made and what happened. Full specifications are available on request.

breadth.heading: A founder does every job at least once.

items.title: Product
items.text: Wrote the full set of product requirements: user stories, acceptance criteria and data rules.

items.title: AI and automation
items.text: Human-in-the-loop design, retrieval-grounded chat and evaluation targets on Google Gemini models.

items.title: Technical delivery
items.text: Managed engineering vendors across the UK, India and the Philippines, and commissioned a code audit of four codebases.

items.title: Fundraising and investors
items.text: Raised £1.6 million in equity and debt, reported to investors every month and built the 2026–2030 business plan.

items.title: Team
items.text: Hired and led a peak team of 18 across three countries, in sales, marketing, support and engineering.

items.title: Finance and operations
items.text: Ran bookkeeping, financial reporting, R&D tax credit claims and grant applications.

items.title: Safeguarding and data
items.text: Built the safeguarding framework and the access and GDPR rules for children's data.

items.title: Partnerships
items.text: Delivered free group tutoring to disadvantaged pupils in Ireland with the charity Teach One, Save One.

now.heading: I still build with my own hands.
now.intro: I write, test and run these myself, in daily use for my teaching practice.

items.title: Post-lesson workflow
items.text: A lesson transcript becomes a summary, a filed record, a tracker update and a draft email to parents, with no manual steps.

lessons.heading: Six things I would tell my 2019 self.

items.title: Ship the simple version first.
items.text: Our first platform had too many features, and many were never needed. I would go to market sooner with less, and let customers tell me what to add.

items.title: Hire slowly, and never out of pressure.
items.text: We grew the team too fast, too early, and under stress I hired reactively. Now I hire for a need I can already see, not one I hope for.

items.title: Only accept accountability that comes with authority.
items.text: For too long I answered for outcomes I did not have the power to change. I now check that the two match before I say yes, and I put the right protections in place on day one.

items.title: Say the hard thing early.
items.text: There were times I stayed quiet when I should have pushed back. A problem raised early is small. Raised late, it is expensive.

items.title: Write everything down.
items.text: Keep a record of decisions every week and every month. It keeps you honest, and it is the first thing you reach for when things get hard.

items.title: No company is worth your health.
items.text: Years without a real break left me tired, reactive and a worse leader. I now treat rest, and knowing when to change course, as part of the job.

contact.heading: Give me a hard problem and a customer.
contact.text: I am looking for a full-time role in AI product or deployment. London based, open to relocation. I work in English, German and Spanish.
